title: Response to Risks from Frontier AI Models with Potential to Steal Data, Disrupt Critical Infrastructure and Exploit Software Vulnerabilities
what_it_is: Response to Risks from Frontier AI Models with Potential to Steal Data, Disrupt Critical Infrastructure and Exploit Software Vulnerabilities

sections.label: Frontier AI cybersecurity threats review
sections.summary: Asked what the Ministry assesses about cybersecurity threats from frontier AI models and whether Singapore's frameworks are being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Digital Development and Information in light of recent reports on frontier AI models, such as Anthropic's Mythos with advanced capabilities to autonomously identify and exploit software vulnerabilities (a) what is the Ministry's assessment of the potential cybersecurity threats posed by such models; and (b) whether the Government is reviewing Singapore's current cybersecurity frameworks and safeguards to address these emerging risks.

sections.label: Monitoring AI threats with partners
sections.summary: The Ministry says the capability is not a sudden step jump and it monitors the space with international partners and agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: It is not suddenly a step jump or a discontinuous capability that we are not prepared for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We have been monitoring this space for some time and are actively working with international partners, both technology companies developing those AI frontier models as well as governmental organisations, on these threats, including those from intelligence and security agencies.

sections.label: Supporting SMEs on cybersecurity
sections.summary: Resources help SMEs do self-checks, follow CSA guidelines, and have cybersecurity hygiene baked into pre-approved SME Go Digital solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Thirdly, we are mindful that SMEs may not have such capabilities and we deployed different resources supporting them to: firstly do a self-check, a hygiene check, on their own systems through the various cyber essential marks and trust marks – they can look at the guidelines published by CSA; secondly, even as SMEs digitalise and adopt AI technology in their organisations, you want to make sure they are safe and there are guidelines in place for them to think about how to deploy AI solutions in their organisations and in their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And through programmes like SMEs Go Digital, where we work with our industry partners providing these technology solutions and pre-approve them for support, we make sure those basic cybersecurity hygiene practices are baked into those systems.

sections.label: Monitoring AI trend over time
sections.summary: The trend has been monitored and acted on for some time, covering not just one model but open-source models too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Because this is a trend that we have seen for some time, and we have been monitoring the trend and taking action for period of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And it is not just about a single model but broadly, even open-source models, we have built up capabilities over time and within matter of months because of how fast AI technology is developing.

sections.label: Visits to 11 CII sectors
sections.summary: The speaker says all 11 critical information infrastructure sectors have been visited over the past months and year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In this House, during the Budget and Committee of Supply speeches, I shared with the House that I have been visiting every of the CII sectors – 11 critical information infrastructure sectors – over the past months and year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I am pleased to share with everyone that I have completed all 11.

sections.label: Sharing threat intelligence with CII
sections.summary: Government and CSA will share selected threat intelligence with selected CII owners to help detect advanced persistent threat actors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Lastly, I must also say that we have been working very closely with all of the CII sectors, I shared in this House during the Committee of Supply debates that the Government and CSA are leaning forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We will share selected threat intelligence information with selected CII owners so that they can better monitor and detect threats against them, especially from advanced persistent threat actors.
